_sources.discrepancies: NCSL classifies DE as 'non-photo ID requested' — voters provide name and address; poll workers may ask for a document showing name and address but it is not strictly required. Registration deadline is the fourth Saturday before the election per DE law. 2026-06-10: Corrected the primary date to September 15, 2026 (was listed as September 12, a Saturday) and the primary registration deadline to August 22 per elections.delaware.gov. Corrected early voting: Delaware HAS offered early in-person voting since 2022 (upheld after the Higgin litigation) — this file previously said it had none; primary early voting September 2–13, general October 22 – November 1. Also corrected absentee rules: the 2022 no-excuse vote-by-mail statute was struck down (Higgin v. Albence, Del. 2022), so absentee voting requires a constitutional excuse.

earlyVoting.notes: Early voting for the September 15 primary runs September 2–13, 2026 (closed September 6–7 for the Labor Day holiday; hours vary by day — schedule per the Department of Elections, subject to change). Early voting sites: https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/votinglocations.shtml

Early voting for the November 3 general election runs October 22 – November 1, 2026 (hours vary by day) at designated early voting sites in each county. Sites: https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/votinglocations.shtml
Delaware offers early in-person voting for at least 10 days before an election at designated sites in each county. Absentee voting requires a qualifying reason under the Delaware Constitution.

acceptedIds: Any document showing name and address (utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, etc.)
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Delaware does not have a statewide ban on phones in polling places. Voters may not photograph their ballot or interfere with other voters. No electioneering within 50 feet of a polling place.
additionalRules: Non-photo ID requested but not required. Poll workers may ask for a document showing name and address.
Closed primary: only voters registered with a party may vote in that party's primary. Unregistered or independent voters may not participate.

Absentee voting requires a qualifying reason under the Delaware Constitution (e.g., work or occupation, sickness or disability, vacation absence, religious tenets). Early in-person voting is available for at least 10 days before an election.

eligibility: In the public service of the United States or Delaware (or a spouse/dependent residing with them)
Cannot appear at the polls because of the nature of their business or occupation
Absent from the district while on vacation
Religious tenets or teachings conflict with voting in person
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: 4 days before the election (received by county department of elections)
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the county department of elections by 8 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive at the county election office by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Postmarks do not count.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Delaware has a closed primary (Del. Code Title 15, §3101A). Only voters registered with a political party may vote in that party's primary. Unaffiliated voters are not permitted to participate in a partisan primary.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Delaware tiene una primaria cerrada (Del. Code Title 15, §3101A). Solo los votantes registrados en un partido político pueden votar en la primaria de ese partido. Los votantes sin afiliación no pueden participar en una primaria partidista.
